reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the premise that edge dislocations dominate deformation in these alloys, but provides no specific support for the super-jogging mechanism, its link to a strength plateau, or the predicted effects of annealing on dislocation mobility and thermoelastic response.
premises: Edge dislocations dominate plastic deformation in BCC refractory HEAs at elevated temperatures
Thermally activated super-jogging of edge dislocations retards their glide
Retarded edge dislocation glide causes a yield strength plateau and near temperature-independent elastic response
Reducing edge dislocation density/pinning via annealing enhances their mobility
Enhanced edge dislocation mobility weakens the strength plateau and increases temperature sensitivity of properties
